'''Nigel Boston''' (July 20, 1961 – March 31, 2024) was a British-American mathematician, who made notable contributions to [[algebraic number theory]], [[group theory]], and [[arithmetic geometry]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS :: Notices of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202506/noti3188/noti3188.html |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=www.ams.org |language=en}}</ref>

==Biography==
Boston attended [[Harvard University]], earning his [[doctorate]] in 1987, under supervision of [[Barry Mazur]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.wisc.edu/~boston/cv.pdf|title=Curriculum Vitae &ndash; Nigel Boston|website=www.math.wisc.edu|access-date=April 8, 2024}}</ref> He was a Professor [[Emeritus]] at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-10.</ref>

Boston died on March 31, 2024, at the age of 62.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://math.wisc.edu/2024/04/03/in-memoriam-nigel-boston/|title= In Memoriam: Nigel Boston|publisher=Department of Mathematics, University of Wisconsin–Madison|website=math.wisc.edu|date=April 3, 2024|access-date=April 8, 2024}}</ref>
